mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate indicates tight monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1600 thousand units signals reduced consumer demand in the housing market, which may lead to broader economic weakness and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST falls below 1600 but the S&P 500 still shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) combined with slowing payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates labor market weakness, which may lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE increases and PAYEMS slows but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals supply chain weaknesses, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is negative but the S&P 500 still shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures, which may lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL exceeds 4% but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases but the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (UNRATE) combined with slowing payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates labor market weakness, which may lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE increases and PAYEMS slows but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) below 2% annualized signals economic weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is below 2% but the S&P 500 still shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
